note: Planar materials from the GM Binder 'Fantasy Metals Compendium' (external homebrew, scanned per user request). Original creative content, not reproducing any official sourcebook — unlike the companion 'Official Plants Lists' page, which was deliberately excluded (see IMPLEMENTATION_TRACKER.md).

entries.name: Inferno Crystal
entries.summary: An extremely volatile crystal of pure plasma, native to the Elemental Plane of Fire.
entries.body: An extremely volatile crystalline material formed from pure plasma. Pure plasma on a scale hundreds of times larger than the crystal will immediately erupt from any broken sample — handled by only the most careful (or reckless) artificers. Used for fire-based enchantments and ammunition.

entries.name: Prismatic Ice
entries.summary: A material that cannot change state or temperature, native to the Elemental Plane of Water.
entries.body: Cannot change state or temperature under any circumstance. Freezes creatures on contact and resists heat extremely effectively. Workable like metal, but only with great difficulty.

entries.name: Aerialite
entries.summary: A light sky-blue metal from the Elemental Plane of Air that grants flight and range.
entries.body: A light sky-blue metal with powerful magic, native to the Elemental Plane of Air. Armor made from it grants greatly increased jump height or a limited flying speed; weapons gain greatly increased range, or the capacity for flight.

entries.name: Gaia Geode
entries.summary: A nearly perfect magical conductor from the Elemental Plane of Earth that shakes the ground it touches.
entries.body: A nearly perfect magical conductor, opaque gray, native to the Elemental Plane of Earth. Its presence in contact with the ground causes massive tectonic disturbances — devastating to armor, and a powerful tool for controlling earth creatures.

entries.name: Chlorophyte
entries.summary: A living, glowing material from the Feywild that implants devouring spores.
entries.body: A dark green living material from the Feywild that glows brighter in sunlight. Implants spores that eat away at opponents and spread over time — left unchecked, it can devour the entire being or object it has taken hold of.

entries.name: Voidmetal
entries.summary: A metal infused with Shadowfell darkness that grants stealth and near-invisibility.
entries.body: Infused with and strengthened by the shadows of the Shadowfell. Spreads darkness and cuts through lit areas as a weapon. The strongest items forged from it can shift between visible and invisible at the user's will; armor grants a natural stealthiness and near-invisibility in darkness.

entries.name: Cosmilite
entries.summary: A purple-glowing metal harder than adamantine, formed over eons in orbit.
entries.body: Harder and more stubborn than adamantine, with a higher melting point and a faint purple glow — extremely dense and hard. Formed by eons of orbiting the sun in an elliptical pattern before falling to the Material Plane.

entries.name: Etherplasm
entries.summary: A translucent, ever-sublimating solid from the Ethereal Plane that can harm ethereal creatures.
entries.body: A gelatinous, translucent gray solid from the Ethereal Plane that constantly undergoes sublimation — small samples wisp away in seconds, larger amounts in minutes. Weapons forged from it can damage creatures on the Ethereal plane; armor allows physical interaction with, but not damage from, ethereal creatures.

entries.name: Prismetal
entries.summary: A multicolored metal from the Astral Plane whose properties depend on which of the Outer Planes each color channels.
entries.body:
A multicolored metal from the Astral Plane, its effects varying by which Outer Plane each embedded color channels. A sample may carry anywhere from two to eight colors at once — more colors, exponentially rarer.

**Number of colors (1d100):** 1-55 two, 56-75 three, 76-85 four, 86-90 five, 91-95 six, 96-99 seven, 100 eight.

**Color origin (1d8):** 1 Red — the Nine Hells, 2 Orange — the Abyss, 3 Yellow — Limbo, 4 Green — Hades, 5 Blue — Mechanus, 6 Indigo — Arborea, 7 Violet — Elysium, 8 White — Mount Celestia.

entries.name: Hallowed Steel
entries.summary: A platinum-colored metal from Mount Celestia, blessed against evil and volatile in evil hands.
entries.body: A bright platinum-colored metal from Mount Celestia, blessed to protect from evil. It naturally shifts anyone holding it toward the Lawful Good alignment, and turns volatile in the grip of a sufficiently evil creature.

entries.name: Idyllium
entries.summary: A metal from Bytopia that appears as the observer's ideal of beauty and slowly erodes their self-control.
entries.body: Appears to each observer as their own ideal vision of beauty and desirability, drawn from Bytopia. Steadily decreases the observer's impulse control; long-term exposure causes obsessive urges to keep and protect it, or to obtain more. Enables the most powerful mind-control, seduction, or domination-themed magic items.

entries.name: Heart Stones
entries.summary: Spherical red-pink stones from Elysium that induce total euphoric relaxation.
entries.body: Spherical, naturally red or pink, and slightly translucent, drawn from Elysium. Contact induces a full-body relaxation reaction, rendering the user satiated and in a state of euphoria. Worked into a weapon or armor, they cause the target to lose the will to fight.

entries.name: Clay of Life
entries.summary: A living clay from the Beastlands that can be shaped into true living creatures.
entries.body: A clay from the Beastlands capable of creating living, sentient, intelligent beings — only beasts and monstrosities. The purity of the sample determines the intelligence of the created being; pure samples can create beings rivalling dragons or even tarrasques. Small samples are enough for a Staff of True Polymorph or a Robe of Shapechange.

entries.name: Ivorite
entries.summary: A gold-and-platinum metal from Arcadia that grants unnatural command over beasts.
entries.body: Bridges organic and inorganic, glimmering in gold and platinum, drawn from Arcadia. Gives the user an unnatural control over beasts and monstrosities — used in items such as Tridents of Fish Command.

entries.name: Valhallium
entries.summary: A metal from Ysgard sharper and deadlier than any other, but nearly impossible to enchant.
entries.body: Can be sharpened finer than any other metal, protects greater than any other, and deals death more easily than any other — drawn from Ysgard. Cannot hold enchantments in any form but the most minimal and basic. Armor made from it negates all but the most powerful attacks; weapons all but ignore the strongest armor.

entries.name: Mechanite
entries.summary: An unworkable metal from Mechanus that yields impossible, precise enhancements.
entries.body: Impossible to work with — its form is absolute and unmalleable, produced only by portals to Mechanus over months or years. Comes pre-formed as tools, weapons, armor, or household items, each bearing unique, extremely useful, and seemingly impossible enhancements. Understanding and using mechanite requires high intelligence.

entries.name: Meld
entries.summary: An amorphous material from Limbo, shapeable at will into any item the wielder imagines.
entries.body: As unpredictable as it is powerful, drawn from Limbo. Can be shaped at-will to its wielder's demands, becoming any size, shape, or manner of item. The power of meld is limited only by the imagination of the wielder.

entries.name: Acher Obsidian
entries.summary: A never-dulling, fey-repelling obsidian from Acheron that shatters under blunt force.
entries.body: Forms in perfect polyhedrons from cooling lava on Acheron. Never dulls, and cuts through nearly any material with little resistance. Naturally repels — and is especially effective in combat against — fey and celestials. Armor made from it strongly resists piercing or slashing damage, but the material itself is brittle and can be broken with enough blunt force.

entries.name: Shrieking Steel
entries.summary: A steel from Pandemonium infected by mad souls, striking the mind as hard as the body.
entries.body: Created from ores infected by "shriekers" — mad souls of Pandemonium. Creatures nearby can feel strong mental disturbances; prolonged exposure without proper safety equipment quickly leads to a loss of sanity. It strikes the mind as hard as the body, and armor forged from it strongly repels enemies from attacking or making contact.

entries.name: Hellstone
entries.summary: A softly glowing red metal from the Nine Hells, explosive near holy magic or fresh water.
entries.body: A softly glowing red metal with fluctuating brightness, native to the Nine Hells. Darkens to a black, matte appearance with cracks of red when exposed to air — and grows brittle once darkened. Reacts violently and explodes when exposed to holy magic or fresh water. Its black flames are the only flames in the known planes that can burn devils; weapons let their wielders sear through devils with ease, and arrows forged from it can trigger explosions on impact.

entries.name: Styxium
entries.summary: An unremarkable black metal from Gehenna with a deep connection to the Weave.
entries.body: A black metal with rather unremarkable physical properties, drawn from Gehenna, but with a strong connection to the Weave — best used as a base for magic items, especially those dealing with spellcasting or spell storing.

entries.name: Daemon Iron
entries.summary: Iron slowly corrupted by Hades' magic that saps emotion and identity from those nearby.
entries.body: Imported iron slowly influenced by the magic of Hades, saps all emotion and identity out of those who are near it. Weapons forged from it cause powerful amnesia effects; armor makes its wearer immune to several kinds of mind-altering magic — though prolonged wear slowly reduces the wearer's own emotional capacity.

fields.location: Hades (Neutral Good / True Neutral / Neutral Evil)

entries.name: Titanium (Carceri)
entries.summary: A titan's gift, corrupted on Carceri into a metal that rots flesh and devastates celestials.
entries.body: A gift from the Titans, originally used in the ancient god-wars — the samples now found on Carceri have been infected by that plane's evil energies. Blades made from it cause deep, necrotic gashes that rot away flesh almost instantly; armor inflicts necrosis on enemy contact, with greatly increased effectiveness against celestials. Legendary pure titanium items are said to have been used to combat even the gods themselves.

entries.name: Aximium
entries.summary: A near-sentient black material from the Abyss formed from the souls of dying demons, which corrupts anyone who wields it.
entries.body:
An amorphous black material that can only be described as corrupted, evil, and nearly sentient, formed from the dying souls of thousands of demons in the Abyss. Users of items forged from it experience amplified strength, pain tolerance, and endurance, and become overcome with euphoria for battle.

Prolonged use corrupts the wielder: after roughly two weeks, aggressive behavior sets in; after five weeks, insanity; after two months, the wielder is completely overcome by demonic tendencies. The strongest samples can form themselves into a weapon with no outside intervention, and can communicate with anyone who makes physical contact.
